key_insight: Open-weight, locally deployable LLM agents can perform much of the routine code-heavy work needed for longitudinal data preparation without sending sensitive data to the cloud.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical path for privacy-preserving, AI-assisted data engineering in governance-restricted research environments using consumer-grade hardware.
method: Built an open-source benchmark with curated ground-truth cleaning scripts for six waves of a British cohort study.
Defined 20 longitudinal data-preparation tasks, including category harmonization and multi-wave merging.
Automated evaluation of model-generated R code and the resulting data outputs.
evidence_signal: Across 20 tasks covering 102 variables, the best 31–35B open-weight models nearly saturated the benchmark, reaching up to 87.9% average task completion.
watch_item: Performance is strong but still depends on task complexity and reliable local execution, so sensitive research workflows will need careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
